- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +10% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 3–5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; if forecast is >15% above recent 18d average, reduce by 5–8%.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often fails to capture momentum; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 3–5 days.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is >10% below forecast, check if sentiment was negative in prior 5 days — if yes, model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 3–7%.
